Goa is India's smallest state by area and a former Portuguese colony on the western coast of the Indian peninsula. It is bounded by Maharashtra to the north and Karnataka to the east and south, with the Arabian Sea to the west.

Panaji (also spelled Panjim) is the capital of Goa. Vasco da Gama is the largest city. The state is divided into two districts: North Goa and South Goa.

Portuguese rule lasted from 1510 until 1961, when Goa was annexed by India through Operation Vijay. Goa became a full state of India in 1987. Konkani is the official language. English, Hindi, Marathi, and Portuguese are also widely used.

Goa's coastline, laterite plateaus, and monsoon-green hinterland shape its culture. Basilica of Bom Jesus in Old Goa holds the relics of St. Francis Xavier and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the churches and convents of Old Goa. Hindu temples such as Mangeshi and Shantadurga sit in Ponda taluka.

The state is known for beaches (Calangute, Baga, Palolem, Agonda), spice plantations, feni (a cashew or coconut spirit), seafood, and a music culture that ranges from mando to trance. Tourism is a major part of the economy, alongside mining historically, pharmaceuticals, and a growing builder/startup scene.

Panaji (also spelled Panjim) is the capital of Goa. Vasco da Gama is the largest city. The state is divided into two districts: North Goa and South Goa.

The state is known for beaches (Calangute, Baga, Palolem, Agonda), spice plantations, feni (a cashew or coconut spirit), seafood, and a music culture that ranges from mando to trance. Builders must ship an end-to-end pipeline: a user speaks a question, speech is transcribed, relevant context is retrieved from a provided dataset, and a grounded answer is returned.

Required shape: Voice input → Speech-to-text → Chunking/Retrieval (vector DB) → Answer generation.

The dataset for the RAG pipeline is ai4bharat/MSMARCO-XI on Hugging Face — MS MARCO translated into Indic languages.

Speech-to-text must use either Sarvam or ElevenLabs. Vaani uses ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime.

Chunking must be engineered: multiple strategies, overlap, semantic versus fixed-size splitting, and metadata-aware indexing. A single naive fixed-size split is not enough.

Latency target: chunking is offline. Online retrieval plus generation should complete in under 200 milliseconds. Submissions must report P50, P70, and P100 latency across many test queries.

The model must run inside a harness — structured orchestration with tool calls, retries, structured input/output, and error recovery — not a raw prompt-in, text-out call.

Guardrails are required: off-topic queries, unsafe inputs, hallucination checks, and answers that are not grounded in retrieved context. The system must know when not to answer.

Konkani (कोंकणी / Konknni) is the official language of Goa. It is an Indo-Aryan language of the Konkan coast, written in Devanagari in official Goa use, and also in Romi (Latin) script among many Catholic Goans. Kannada, Malayalam, and Perso-Arabic scripts appear in other Konkani communities.

A common Konkani greeting is "Dev borem korum" — "May God do good" / a blessing hello. Replies include "Dev borem korum" in return. "Deu boro dis dium" wishes a good day. "Hai" and "hói" are informal yes. "Naka" is no.

Konkani is closely related to Marathi. Speakers often understand Marathi; MSMARCO-XI does not include a Konkani split, so Vaani indexes Marathi as the nearest Indic neighbor and keeps a dedicated Goa knowledge pack for local facts and greetings.

Goan English is a distinct coastal variety. Goan Hindi is widely understood because of tourism and internal migration. Vaani answers in the language the user spoke: English, Hindi, or a Konkani greeting acknowledged in kind.

Vaani (वाणी) means "voice" or "speech" in Sanskrit and many Indic languages. The product is a living voice that only speaks from evidence.
